topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students and contextualizes the lecture on complement within the immunology curriculum.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the general organization and core molecular machinery that govern the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinct pathways through which complement recognizes pathogens and triggers surface C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms by which activated complement neutralizes pathogens and coordinates immune defense.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the mechanisms that prevent complement from activating on and damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the pathological and clinical consequences of deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evolved mechanisms to evade complement-mediated immunity, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic in the immunology series.
